headline: NAB's Group cash-basis cost-to-income ratio rose 80 bps (0.8 ppt) in FY25, from 46.5% at Sep 24 to 47.3% at Sep 25 (results book KPI table). On the statutory basis it rose 110 bps, from 48.5% to 49.6%. The rise reflects negative jaws: operating income grew 2.9% (net operating income $20,813m vs $20,236m) while operating expenses grew 4.6% ($9,848m vs $9,413m), so expenses outran income and pushed the ratio up. Expense growth of 4.6% includes $130m of payroll review and remediation costs; excluding these, expenses rose 3.2%. The bank does not publish a dedicated CTI bridge chart; the driver split below is built from the jaws (income vs expense growth) and the bank's own primary FY24-to-FY25 operating expense walk.

drivers.narrative: Operating expenses rose $435m or 4.6% (Sep 24 $9,413m to Sep 25 $9,848m), outrunning income growth and raising the ratio. The bank's primary FY24-to-FY25 expense walk decomposes the increase: salary related +$267m, volume related +$143m, technology & investment +$213m, depreciation & amortisation +$42m, other +$131m, payroll review and remediation +$130m, partially offset by productivity -$420m and EU -$71m. Excluding $130m payroll review and remediation, expenses rose 3.2%.

Operating income grew 2.9% (net operating income $20,236m to $20,813m), slower than expenses, so income growth contributed negatively to the ratio (lowering it relative to what expense growth alone would imply). Net interest income rose $644m or 3.8% (underlying +$718m or 4.3% ex economic hedges) on higher average interest earning assets and NIM; other operating income fell $67m or 1.9% on customer-related remediation and business disposals.

drivers.bank_label: Notable and restructuring items on either side
drivers.narrative: Payroll review and remediation costs of $130m (included in the expense walk) and customer-related remediation charges of $67m (in other operating income) are notable items on the expense and income sides respectively. The bank does not quantify their separate effect on the CTI ratio, so no ppt contribution is claimed; they are reported within the income and expense drivers above.

notable_items: Customer-related remediation charges $67m in other operating income

disagreements.explanation: The cash and statutory CTI differ because statutory includes hedging/fair value volatility, amortisation of acquired intangibles and acquisitions/disposals items that cash earnings excludes. The primary basis is cash.

limitations: The bank does not publish a dedicated CTI bridge/walk chart in either the results book or the investor presentation. The driver split is therefore built from the jaws (income vs expense growth) and the bank's own primary FY24-to-FY25 operating expense walk (investor presentation p25), not from a CTI-specific decomposition. The ppt contributions for income and expense growth are my own arithmetic from the disclosed levels, capped at 80 confidence.

The read_chart tool misread the 'FY25 v FY24 drivers of cash earnings change (%)' chart on results book p5 as a CTI walk (start 1390, end 1220); that chart is actually a cash earnings change decomposition (Income +2.9%, Expenses +4.6%, Underlying profit +1.3%), not a CTI bridge, so it was not used.

The investor presentation does not contain a Group KPI table with the CTI; the CTI movement is corroborated only by the results book KPI table (p15). The expense walk on presentation p25 corroborates the expense side.
The bank does not quantify the separate effect of notable items (payroll review and remediation, customer-related remediation) on the CTI ratio, so no ppt contribution is claimed for them.
Research stopped early: the tool-call budget (80 calls) was reached, so the evidence behind this answer is less complete than a full run's.
Capped at 80: expense_growth +0.8 ppt. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
